task: synthetic browser-style target selection with exactly one candidate labelled Apply Now

listwiseOneSequence.description: all candidates rendered as one dynamic choice set in a single Laya sequence

independentBinaryScoring.description: one binary noul sequence per candidate, batched per decision; final candidate chosen by maximum true probability

interpretation: the same checkpoint recovers high-cardinality synthetic target selection when candidates are scored independently
the dominant observed failure is therefore strongly associated with listwise option representation/shared sequence budget rather than a simple lack of semantic recognition
independent scoring removes the hard head_max_len cardinality ceiling and largely removes observed fixed-position attractors
independent scoring introduces approximately linear latency in candidate count
mature retrieve-then-rerank architectures are the primary next candidate because they preserve independent candidate scoring while reducing expensive scorer calls
